original_question: Are there alternatives to inner product expansions for studying logarithmic and Riesz energy asymptotics on the sphere that can replace the present expansion method?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Question 2.3 (Johann Brauchart): "Are there other replacements for inner product expansion?" ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies that the paper is asking for alternatives to the inner-product-expansion method in the study of logarithmic and Riesz energy asymptotics on the sphere, rather than asking for a proof of the Riesz 2-energy conjecture itself or for new identities among asymptotic coefficients. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))
missing_details: The paper works on the unit sphere S^d ⊂ R^(d+1) with respect to the Euclidean distance, not on a general sphere or a different metric space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))
The relevant quantities are the discrete minimal logarithmic energy E_log(S^d;N) and the discrete minimal Riesz energy E_s(S^d;N) for s > 0. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

In the nearby context, "inner product expansion" refers specifically to expanding log(1/||x-y||) as a power series in the inner product ⟨x,y⟩; this is the present method being discussed. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

The section frames this as a methodological question arising from attempts to obtain lower bounds and asymptotic information, including a link between logarithmic energy and Riesz 2-energy via summation by parts. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

Your draft slightly blurs Question 2.3 with neighboring Question 2.2: the paper distinguishes between finding better resummation methods and finding replacements for the inner-product expansion itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or "for all sufficiently large m"-type quantifier appears in this problem; those data are not part of the paper's formulation here. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))
refined_question: For the discrete minimal logarithmic energy E_log(S^d;N) = min_{x_1,...,x_N ∈ S^d} Σ_{i ≠ j} log(1/||x_i-x_j||) and the discrete minimal Riesz energy E_s(S^d;N) = min_{x_1,...,x_N ∈ S^d} Σ_{i ≠ j} ||x_i-x_j||^(−s), with s > 0, on the unit sphere S^d ⊂ R^(d+1) and in the asymptotic regime N → ∞, is there a method that can replace the current expansion of the kernel in powers of the inner product ⟨x,y⟩ and still be effective for studying lower bounds or asymptotic expansions of these energies? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))
justification: The nearest official formulation is Section 2, Question 2.3, not Conjecture 2.1 and not Question 2.2. Section 2 first defines the logarithmic and Riesz energies on S^d, states the N → ∞ asymptotic setting, explains that one possible lower-bound approach is to expand log(1/||x-y||) as a power series in ⟨x,y⟩, gives Lemma 2.1 in that direction, then uses summation by parts to connect logarithmic energy to Riesz 2-energy before stating Conjecture 2.1 and Theorem 2.1. Only then does the paper pose Question 2.3 asking for replacements for inner product expansion. So the faithful stand-alone rewrite should import exactly that local setup and should not broaden the problem beyond Section 2’s methodological scope. The paper does not state an equivalent reformulation of Question 2.3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))
